'''Monta Jerome Ellis''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|m|ɒ|n|t|eɪ}} {{respell|MON|tay}}; born October 26, 1985) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Ellis attended [[Lanier High School (Jackson, Mississippi)|Lanier High School]] in [[Jackson, Mississippi]], where he was a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] and first-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]]. He entered the [[NBA]] directly out of high school, being drafted with the 40th overall pick by the [[Golden State Warriors]] in the [[2005 NBA draft]]. In 2007, he was named the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|NBA Most Improved Player]]. During his career Ellis was one of the best scorers in the league, averaging close to 25 points per game on two occasions.

After six and a half seasons with Golden State, he was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in March 2012; a season and a half with the Bucks was followed by two seasons with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] and finally, two seasons with the [[Indiana Pacers]].

==High school career==
Ellis attended [[Lanier High School (Jackson, Mississippi)|Lanier High School]] in [[Jackson, Mississippi]]. As a senior in 2004–05, at 19 years old, Ellis led Lanier to its second state crown in four years, averaging 38.4 points, 7.9 rebounds, 6.9 assists and 4.5 steals per game for a team that finished 35–2 and No. 3 in the FAB 50 national rankings. During his senior season, Ellis scored 65 points against [[Greenwood High School (Mississippi)|Greenwood]].<ref name=facts>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/gallery/11-facts-about-monta-ellis|title=11 Facts About Monta Ellis|work=NBA.com|date=August 10, 2015|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> The schools met again later that season,<ref name="facts" /> where Ellis had 72 points, a mark tied for second on the all-time state charts. He also had 46 points against [[Oak Hill Academy (Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]]. For his efforts, Ellis was named 2005 EA SPORTS National Player of the Year and ''[[Parade (magazine)|Parade]]'' co-Player of the Year with [[Greg Oden]].<ref name=rewind>{{cite web|last=Huff|first=Doug|url=https://www.espn.com/highschool/rise/basketball/boys/news/story?id=4828700|title=Rewind: Monta Ellis|work=ESPN.com|date=January 17, 2010|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> Ellis led Lanier to a 129–16 record in his four seasons as a starter, winning the 4A state championship in both 2002 (33–5) and 2005 and runner-up finishes in 2003 (31–4) and 2004 (30–5). He finished ranked second in state history with 4,167 points, good for 28.7 points per game.<ref name="rewind" /><ref>{{cite web|last=Abrams|first=Jonathan|url=https://grantland.com/features/the-life-career-milwaukee-bucks-guard-monta-ellis/|title=Monta Ellis Is Probably Shooting Right Now|work=grantland.com|date=April 24, 2013|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref>

Ellis originally committed to [[Mississippi State University]], but later decided to enter the [[NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Katz|first=Andy|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2046200|title=Point guard Ellis will declare for NBA draft|work=ESPN.com|date=April 26, 2005|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Golden State Warriors (2005–2012)===
Ellis was selected with the 40th overall pick (second round) in the [[2005 NBA draft]] by the [[Golden State Warriors]]. He appeared in 46 games as a rookie and made three starts, with all three coming over the last four games of the season. He averaged 6.8 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 1.6 assists in 18.1 minutes per game.<ref name=br06>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/e/ellismo01/gamelog/2006/|title=Monta Ellis 2005–06 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> In the Warriors' season finale on April 19, 2006, Ellis scored a season-high 27 points as Golden State lost 105–102 to the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref name="br06" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=260419026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306043651/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=260419026|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 6, 2019|title=Jazz beat Warriors to salvage winning season|work=ESPN.com|date=April 19, 2006|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref>

Ellis averaged 16.5 points, 4.1 assists, 3.2 rebounds and 1.7 steals in 2006–07, helping the Warriors return to the playoffs after a 12-year absence.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nba_news/monta_ellis_most_improved_player.html|title=Golden State's Monta Ellis Selected Most Improved Player|work=NBA.com|date=April 26, 2007|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> Ellis increased his scoring by 9.7 points from his rookie season, the largest increase in the NBA. Starting 53 of the 77 games he appeared in, Ellis reached double figures in scoring 68 times, including 24 games of 20 or more points.<ref name=mip>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/Monta_Ellis_Most_Improved.html|title=Monta Ellis Named 2006–07 Most Improved Player|work=NBA.com|date=April 26, 2007|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> He scored a season-high 31 points three times, twice in November and once in March.<ref name=br07>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/e/ellismo01/gamelog/2007/|title=Monta Ellis 2006–07 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> On February 24, Ellis recorded a career-high 13 assists against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270224012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180818084019/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270224012|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 18, 2018|title=Clippers end four-game skid, take over eighth place in West|work=ESPN.com|date=February 24, 2007|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> He recorded three or more steals 20 times and had at least five steals three times, including a career-high six against the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] on March 17, 2007.<ref name="mip" /> He was subsequently named the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|NBA Most Improved Player]].<ref name="mip" /> In May, he helped the Warriors defeat the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in six games in the first round of the [[2007 NBA Playoffs|playoffs]], becoming the first No. 8 seed to capture a best-of-seven playoff series.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20070503/DALGSW/recap.html|title=Warriors Upset Mavs to Clinch First-Round Series|work=NBA.com|date=May 3, 2007|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> The Warriors went on to lose in five games to the [[Utah Jazz]] in the second round.[[File:Monta Ellis cropped.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Ellis with the Warriors in April 2008]]
Ellis averaged a career-high 20.2 points, 5.0 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 1.53 steals in 37.9 minutes in 81 games during the 2007–08 season. He ranked 14th in the NBA in field goal percentage (.531, 3rd among all guards), 15th in steals and 25th in scoring.<ref name=contract08>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors_resign_monta_ellis.html|title=Warriors Re-Sign Guard Monta Ellis To Multi-Year Contract|work=NBA.com|date=July 24, 2008|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> He became only the ninth guard in NBA history to shoot 60% from the floor for an entire month in February (.602).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280229009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180323092357/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280229009|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 23, 2018|title=Wright's first-quarter scoring burst gets Warriors on right track|work=ESPN.com|date=February 29, 2008|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> He scored a career-high 39 points on January 24 against the [[New Jersey Nets]] and scored 30-plus points on 12 occasions overall.<ref name="contract08" />

On July 24, 2008, Ellis re-signed with the Warriors to a six-year, $66 million contract.<ref name="contract08" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/warriors-ink-monta-ellis-to-66m-contract-1.702641|title=Warriors ink Monta Ellis to $66M contract|work=cbc.ca|date=July 25, 2008|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> However, in August, he was sidelined for three-plus months after suffering a Grade 3 high ankle sprain, a torn [[Medial ligament of talocrural joint|deltoid ligament]] and a syndesmosis disruption of his left ankle that required surgery.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/ellis_surgery_082708.html|title=Monta Ellis Undergoes Successful Surgery|work=NBA.com|date=August 27, 2008|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> The injuries occurred in a motorized scooter accident, but his mistake was compounded by telling the Warriors he hurt himself playing pickup ball in his native Mississippi, only coming clean about the accident several days later. As a result, he was suspended by the Warriors for 30 games without pay—the approximate number of games he was expected to miss with the injury anyway.<ref>{{cite web|last=Hu|first=Janny|url=https://www.sfgate.com/sports/article/Accident-earns-Ellis-30-game-suspension-3265958.php|title=Accident earns Ellis 30-game suspension|work=sfgate.com|date=October 12, 2008|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3638098|title=Ellis gets 30-game suspension without pay for accident|work=ESPN.com|date=October 12, 2008|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref>

On February 7, he scored a career-high 48 points in a 119–116 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=320207009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306111359/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=320207009|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 6, 2019|title=Kevin Durant, Thunder hold off Warriors despite Monta Ellis' 48 points|work=ESPN.com|date=February 7, 2012|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> On March 12, he was named Western Conference Player of the Week for games played Monday, March 5, through Sunday, March 11. ===Milwaukee Bucks (2012–2013)===
[[File:Monta Ellis Bucks.jpg|thumb|Ellis with the Bucks in March 2013]]

===Dallas Mavericks (2013–2015)===
[[File:Monta ellis mavs1.JPG|thumb|Ellis with the Mavericks in November 2013, being defended by [[Chandler Parsons]].]]
On July 23, 2013, Ellis signed a three-year, $25 million contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|last=MacMahon|first=Tim|url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/nba/story/_/id/9503261/monta-ellis-officially-signs-contract-dallas-mavericks-brandan-wright-agrees-deal|title=Mavericks officially sign Monta Ellis|work=ESPN.com|date=July 23, 2013|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> He joined the Mavericks with questions about his efficiency on offense.<ref name=mavs-debut>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400488885|title=Mavs romp as Monta Ellis shines in Dallas debut|work=ESPN.com|date=October 30, 2013|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> The 2013–14 season saw Ellis start in all 82 games for the Mavericks.<ref name=br1314>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/e/ellismo01/gamelog/2014/|title=Monta Ellis 2013–14 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> In his debut for the Mavericks on October 30, 2013, Ellis scored 32 points in a 118–109 season-opening win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. He was 11 of 17 from the field and had eight assists.<ref name="mavs-debut" /> On November 20, he scored a season-high 37 points in a 123–120 win over the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400489045|title=Mavs overcome Dwight Howard's season-high 33 to repel Rockets|work=ESPN.com|date=November 20, 2013|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> On April 12, 2014, he matched his season high with 37 points in a 101–98 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400490068|title=Dirk Nowitzki, Monta Ellis fuel Mavericks past Suns and into playoffs|work=ESPN.com|date=April 12, 2014|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> He was subsequently named Western Conference Player of the Week for the final week of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pr.nba.com/jeff-teague-monta-ellis-nba-players-of-the-week/|title=Hawks' Jeff Teague, Mavericks' Monta Ellis named NBA Players of the Week|work=NBA.com|date=April 14, 2014|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> The eighth-seeded Mavericks pushed their first-round playoff series against the [[San Antonio Spurs]] to seven games, but ultimately lost 4–3. Over the seven games, Ellis averaged 20.4 points per game.<ref name="br1314" />

On December 2, 2014, Ellis scored 38 points in a 132–129 double-overtime win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400578549|title=Monta Ellis, Mavs overcome Derrick Rose-led Bulls in double OT|work=ESPN.com|date=December 2, 2014|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> On December 20, Ellis equaled his season high with 38 points, including 11 during the final four minutes, as the Mavericks rallied late to beat the Spurs 99–93.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400578689|title=Rajon Rondo collects 6 points, 9 assists as Mavs rally past Spurs|work=ESPN.com|date=December 20, 2014|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> On March 24, 2015, he matched his season high with 38 points in a 101–94 win over the Spurs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400579349|title=Monta Ellis pours in 38 as Mavericks rally in 2nd half to beat Spurs|work=ESPN.com|date=March 24, 2015|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> For the regular season, Ellis averaged 18.9 points to become the first player other than [[Dirk Nowitzki]] to lead the Mavericks in scoring since [[1999–2000 Dallas Mavericks season|1999–2000]].<ref name=opts-out>{{cite web|last1=MacMahon|first1=Tim|last2=Broussard|first2=Chris|url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/nba/story/_/id/13141024/monta-ellis-opts-contract|title=Monta Ellis set for free agency|work=ESPN.com|date=June 24, 2015|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> In the Mavericks' five-game first-round playoff series loss to the Rockets, Ellis averaged 26.0 points per game,<ref name=br1415>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/e/ellismo01/gamelog/2015/|title=Monta Ellis 2014–15 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> including scoring a playoff career-high 34 points in a 130–128 loss in game three<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400790917|title=James Harden, Dwight Howard notch career playoff bests; Rockets up 3–0|work=ESPN.com|date=April 24, 2015|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> and 31 points in a 121–109 win in game four.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400790918|title=J.J. Barea, Al-Farouq Aminu help Mavs push series vs. Rockets to 3–1|work=ESPN.com|date=April 26, 2015|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref>

On June 24, 2015, Ellis decided not to pick up the option for the final year of his contract with the Mavericks, thus becoming a free agent.<ref name="opts-out" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/dallas-mavericks/mavericksheadlines/2015/06/24/monta-ellis-opts-out-of-mavericks-contract-chooses-free-agency|title=Monta Ellis opts out of Mavericks contract, chooses free agency|work=dallasnews.com|date=June 24, 2015|access-date=March 2, 2019|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He underwent surgery on his right knee before the start of free agency, with the procedure described as "minor".<ref>{{cite web|last=Lewis|first=Tom|url=https://www.indycornrows.com/2015/10/27/9621476/monta-ellis-profile-reveals-knee-surgery-prior-to-signing-with-pacers|title=Monta Ellis profile reveals knee surgery prior to signing with Pacers|work=indycornrows.com|date=October 27, 2015|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref>

===Indiana Pacers (2015–2017)===
On July 14, 2015, Ellis signed a four-year, $44 million contract with the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/pacers-sign-veteran-free-agent-monta-ellis|title=Pacers Sign Veteran Free Agent Monta Ellis|work=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2015|access-date=July 14, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Broussard|first1=Chris|last2=Stein|first2=Marc|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13187862/monta-ellis-agrees-sign-indiana-pacers|title=Monta Ellis to sign four-year, $44M deal with Pacers|work=ESPN.com|date=July 2, 2015|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> He appeared in 81 games in [[2015–16 Indiana Pacers season|2015–16]], all as a starter, sitting out only the regular-season finale ahead of the playoffs.<ref name=br1516>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/e/ellismo01/gamelog/2016/|title=Monta Ellis 2015–16 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400829112|title=Solomon Hill scores 25, Pacers beat Bucks 97–92|work=ESPN.com|date=April 13, 2016|access-date=March 2, 2019|quote=...with starters including Paul George and Monta Ellis sitting out.}}</ref> On January 10, 2016, he had a season-high 13 assists in a 107–103 overtime loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400828448|title=Ariza scores 24, Rockets rally to beat Pacers 107–103 in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=January 10, 2016|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> On January 30, Ellis scored a season-high 32 points and had nine rebounds to lead the Pacers to a 109–105 overtime win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400828596|title=Ellis scores 32 points, Pacers beat Nuggets 109–105 in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=January 30, 2016|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> He finished the regular season averaging 13.8 points on 43 percent shooting, including 31 percent from the 3-point line. Turnover prone, he averaged 2.5 [[Turnover (basketball)|turnovers]] during the regular season and 2.4 during the playoffs.<ref>{{cite web|last=Montieth|first=Mark|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/player-review-2016-monta-ellis|title=Player Review 2016: Monta Ellis|work=NBA.com|date=May 23, 2016|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref>

In the Pacers' season opener on October 26, 2016, Ellis recorded 19 points, seven rebounds, seven assists and three steals in a 130–121 overtime win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899379|title=Mavericks vs. Pacers – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=October 26, 2016|access-date=October 26, 2016}}</ref> He failed to surpass that scoring mark for the rest of the season, scoring 19 points twice in November and again in March.<ref name=br1617>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/e/ellismo01/gamelog/2017/|title=Monta Ellis 2016–17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> On December 10, he injured his groin in the first half of the Pacers' comeback win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Gibson|first=Ben|url=https://8points9seconds.com/2016/12/12/monta-ellis-groin-injury/|title=Monta Ellis Will Miss Next 4 Games With Groin Injury|work=8points9seconds.com|date=December 12, 2016|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> He subsequently missed the next eight games with a strained right groin.<ref name="br1617" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899918|title=Wall scores 36 points as Wizards hold off Pacers, 111–105|work=ESPN.com|date=December 28, 2016|access-date=December 28, 2016}}</ref> Upon returning from injury, he lost his starting spot to [[Glenn Robinson III]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Furr|first=William|url=https://8points9seconds.com/2017/01/03/glenn-robinson-iii-vs-monta-ellis/|title=Who Should Start for the Indiana Pacers? Glenn Robinson III Vs Monta Ellis|work=8points9seconds.com|date=January 3, 2017|access-date=March 3, 2019}}</ref> In 74 games, he made 33 starts and averaged 8.5 points, 2.8 rebounds, 3.2 assists, and 1.1 steals in 27.0 minutes per game.<ref name="br1617" />

On July 6, 2017, Ellis was waived by the Pacers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-waive-ellis|title=Pacers Waive Ellis|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2017|access-date=July 6, 2017}}</ref> He was paid by the Pacers through the [[2021–22 Indiana Pacers season|2021–22 season]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/tonyeast/2019/08/28/why-the-indiana-pacers-are-still-paying-monta-ellis/|title = Why the Indiana Pacers Are Still Paying Monta Ellis}}, Forbes Magazine, August 28, 2019</ref>

==Executive career==
On August 7, 2026, it was announced that Ellis would serve as the general manager at [[Alcorn State Braves basketball|Alcorn State]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ex-NBA star Monta Ellis named Alcorn State basketball GM|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/49554748/ex-nba-star-monta-ellis-named-alcorn-state-basketball-gm|access-date=August 8, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Ellis is the son of Marcellus Singleton and Rosa Ellis.<ref name=Buckner>{{cite web|last=Buckner|first=Candace|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2015/10/24/monta-ellis-basketball-my-escape-really-didnt-have-childhood/74334400/|title=Monta Ellis: 'Basketball was my escape. I really didn't have a childhood'|work=IndyStar.com|date=October 24, 2015|access-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref> His older brother Antwain Ellis was his basketball hero growing up.<ref name="Buckner" /> Ellis and his wife, Juanika, have three children.<ref name="facts" /> Ellis is a [[Sneaker collecting|sneakerhead]] and an avid fisherman.<ref name="facts" />
